name: ratified decisions (ADR index)
description: @resonance/core is the root of the dep graph — shared types, Zod schemas, ports; keep logic extraction-ready (ADR-0002, ADR-0003).

content: Define the generated-draft + commit Zod schemas (CreatorProfileDraft, CommitProfileInput) in @resonance/core; @resonance/ai (server) produces, @resonance/ui (client) edits, apps/web validates — same rationale as InterviewMessageSchema. Factor field-limit schemas as module-private consts shared by draft + commit so limits can't drift.

name: discovery contract as a swappable ranking seam
description: The discovery ranking seam is a ONE-METHOD interface in @resonance/core (DiscoveryPort.searchCreators) over Zod query/result schemas; the deep implementation (embed -> status-filtered pgvector ANN -> tag filter -> threshold -> keyset paging -> follow-state resolution) lives entirely in @resonance/db, so web and ui depend on the interface and never on SQL. Four shape decisions carry the depth: (1) the VIEWER IS A SEPARATE PARAMETER, not a query field - the query is parsed from untrusted client input while the viewer is derived server-side, so identity cannot be spoofed through the search box because there is no field to spoof; (2) the narrow query type is DERIVED (CreatorDiscoveryQuerySchema = DiscoveryQuerySchema.extend({kind: z.literal('creators')})) so the creators-only dispatch is compiler-enforced instead of a doc-only invariant, and cannot drift from the parent; (3) the cursor is an OPAQUE string with no codec in core - shipping an encode/decode pair would over-specify the ranker and shrink the set of substitutable adapters; (4) follow MUTATION is deliberately absent from the port - it is not ranking, and including it would force every alternative ranker to reimplement it. The port's INVARIANTS (ordering, threshold, limit, cursor-null semantics, viewer->followState, draft exclusion, throw-don't-return-empty) are documented ON the interface, because the interface is everything a caller must know, not just the type signature. Deletion test: deleting the module makes complexity reappear in two packages at once (web's Server Action and ui's row props each hand-roll and then drift), and ranking stops being swappable - threshold/filter experiments would have to edit the UI. The acceptance proof is a second adapter: a complete in-memory DiscoveryPort in discovery.test.ts driven purely through the interface, implementing all seven invariants rather than just the signature, plus a test that swaps a reversed ranker behind a byte-identical call site.

content: A cross-package CONSTANT belongs in @resonance/core whenever the two packages that need it cannot import each other. The embedding width is the worked example: @resonance/db owns the vector(1024) column and @resonance/ai owns the embedder, but the dependency runs ai -> db, so db can never import ai's EMBEDDING_DIMS and the two could only agree by coincidence. core is the root of the graph (ADR-0003) and is therefore the only place the fact can live once. Ship the guard with the constant, not just the number: assertEmbeddingDims(embedding) throws the named, coded EmbeddingDimensionError so every call site produces an identical message and code (locality), and a wrong-width vector fails loudly instead of degrading into an empty pgvector result that reads as 'no matches' rather than 'misconfigured embedder' (ADR-0010). Two review lessons from landing it: (a) do not write 'the one place X is defined' in a docstring while the pre-existing duplicates are still in place - state the intended end state, name the remaining copies, and cite the follow-up seed, or the doc gate correctly flags the overclaim; (b) never cite a seed id you have not created - the doc gate resolves seed anchors against .seeds/ and a fabricated id is a broken anchor.

name: typed-vs-carried corpus contract
description: When a package must host an external author's document whose structure exceeds what the product consumes, type only the parts a consumer reads and carry the rest verbatim behind one recursive data schema (CorpusValueSchema: the JSON/YAML value domain). In @resonance/core's Weave OS contracts, headers, principles, limitations, rules, heuristics, flow map, stages, captures, actions and output constraints are typed because the resolver/prompt composer/validator/evaluator read them; every other authored block lands in a 'guidance' record. This keeps the shared vocabulary from absorbing one creator flow's specifics (which would make it unable to host a member flow), avoids inventing schema for content nobody parses, and leaves the specified-vs-implemented gap deliberate and measurable rather than hidden. A block graduates to a typed field when a consumer appears. The carrier is NOT an 'any' escape hatch: it rejects functions and undefined.

title: Weave OS: child-side inheritance, separate limitation type, and 16 composed evaluation dimensions
rationale: Three shapes in @resonance/core that four packages (weave-os, db, ai, evolution) build against, each chosen against a plausible alternative. (1) INHERITANCE IS CHILD-SIDE ONLY. The designer's docs express the edge both ways; parent-side storage (philosophy.architecture.inherited_by) would force every new root file to edit the philosophy, whose own evolution_policy sets change_threshold: exceptional. CorpusInheritedBy is a derived-view TYPE with deliberately no schema — making it parseable would make it storable, i.e. a second source of truth that can disagree. A test asserts no schema has an inheritedBy key. Same reasoning kills an authored 'layer' field: layer is derived from file type via CORPUS_FILE_LAYERS. (2) LIMITATION IS ITS OWN RECORD TYPE, not a principle with an empty rubric. The philosophy's twelve 'Weave will never...' items are boolean invariants; a 'mostly held' limitation is a breach, so scoring one on the 0-3 principle scale would let a violation be averaged away. They surface as LimitationVerdict (held: boolean), never as a scored dimension. (3) THE 16 DIMENSIONS COMPOSE, they are not two competing lists. The engine spec names 10 evaluation dimensions and the principles doc names 7 principles: principle_alignment is one of the 10 and decomposes into 7 principle sub-scores, the other 9 are process/outcome measures, so an evaluation scores 7+9=16. Expressed in the types (ProcessDimension = Exclude<EvaluationDimension, typeof COMPOSITE_DIMENSION> plus 'satisfies'), not in a comment. There is deliberately NO roll-up from the 7 back to a single principle_alignment value — mean vs min vs weighted is a judgement the source documents do not settle, and baking one in would fix it for every consumer.

content: A schema for an external author's spec must FAIL on anything the source documents do not attest, rather than widen to accommodate it. In @resonance/core's EvolutionPolicySchema the three governance fields (architectAccess, directModification, changeThreshold) are SINGLE-MEMBER Zod enums because the corpus attests exactly one value each — 'routine' or 'allowed' is rejected loudly, and widening the scale is a deliberate schema change made with the designer. Same rule elsewhere: CORPUS_FILE_STATUSES holds exactly the three statuses the corpus uses; a flow's appliedPrinciples is typed as ids (not prose) so an unresolved reference fails instead of reading as documentation. The inverse also holds — do not tighten past what the source determines: FlowMap branch targets are NOT resolved against stage ids, because the authored flow branches to targets absent from its own sequence, and requiring resolution would reject the designer's own file. Loud failure is the designed behaviour for this project; silently mapping or inventing semantics corrupts the foundation on day one.

name: optional-query-text-as-second-ranking-signal
description: To let one ranking seam serve both 'search for this text' and 'rank for this viewer', make the query TEXT optional rather than adding a second port method or a sibling port. DiscoveryPort keeps exactly one method; the query vector gains a second source (embedded search text, or the viewer's stored interest embedding) and callers cannot tell which was used. Two rules make it safe: absent and empty-string must stay DIFFERENT at the schema boundary (absent = personalize, empty string = malformed search, still fails .min(1)), and 'no signal to personalize on' must return an EMPTY page, never an unranked dump — those are different answers and only the first is honest. Declared as invariant 8 on the interface and exercised by the in-test fake adapter, not merely typed. This is what resonance-7890 meant when it required Slice A/B to keep ranking behind a small swappable seam.
